newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-SKAARDAL FASTEST IN ACCIDENT-FREE TRAINING.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SKAARDAL FASTEST IN ACCIDENT-FREE TRAINING.

text.p: Norway's Atle Skaardal posted the fastest time in an accident-free World Cup downhill training run on the demanding and dreaded Streif piste in Kitzbuehel on Wednesday.
The 3,200 metres long course with a vertical drop of 860 metres, considered one of the most difficult on the men's alpine ski circuit, surprisingly claimed no victims on a sunny and mild day.

Last year, Norway's overall World Cup champion Lasse Kjus and Austrian's Andreas Schifferer and Josef Strobl all had to be airlifted to hospital with concussion after crashing heavily during training.
On Wednesday, racers were pleased with conditions on the Hahnenkamm mountain, which will host a two-run sprint downhill on Friday and a regular full-length downhill on Saturday.
"The piste is in excellent conditions. It's hard and icy. It was a good training run," said Frenchman Luc Alphand, winner of last season's overall downhill World Cup.
Alphand, who topped the podium at downhills in Val Gardena and Bormio this season, clocked the second fastest time of one minute 55.96 seconds, 0.18 seconds behind Skaardal's 1:55.78.
Austria's only winner of a downhill this winter, Fritz Strobl, was third quickest in 1:55.98, ahead of compatriots Patrick Ortlieb (1:56.27) and Guenther Mader (1:56.34).
In-form Italian Kristian Ghedina, current leader of the downhill World Cup and winner of three races this season, took it easy on Wednesday and posted the 28th best time.
"It's been a long season so far. I didn't want to wear myself out so I decided to take it easy today. Tommorrow I will try harder," he said.
"I am concentrating primarily on the world championships (in Sestriere in February)," he added. "It's not often a skier has the chance to become world champion in his own country."
A third downhill training run is scheduled for Thursday.
